# Manager liveness & worker process audit (Hermes Manager chats)

Lessons from S09 lane 2026-08-22/23 (MotionForge2D). Scope: when THIS chat is the HERMES MANAGER dispatching/resuming background worker sessions (hermes.exe chat -q ... --pass-session-id -Q), not when acting as the worker.

## The false-death incident (what happened)
- Old T01 worker (proc_f24cb4aef494, pid 2320) was declared "dead ~00:31" based on: MSYS `ps` showing no matching PID + dispatch.log frozen at N lines for many minutes.
- Reality: worker ran until ~04:13, finished TASK_SUBMITTED (models.py additive edit, migration c9d0e1f2a3b4, 48 tests ×2, REPORT.md).
- Root causes of the misread:
  1. MSYS `ps` cannot map Windows PIDs after the bash wrapper process exits — the hermes.exe child keeps running invisible to ps.
  2. dispatch.log freezes for tens of minutes between buffer flushes; "no growth in 8 min" is NOT death evidence.
  3. Between long sleep-polls, intermediate log-size growth was skipped; only endpoints were compared.
- Cost: ~3h of wrong state, a registry CORRECTION row, and a near-miss on double-dispatching T00 lanes over a live writer.

## Correct liveness protocol
1. **Wrapper EXIT marker is authoritative for death — and must be read at EOF only**: the dispatcher appends `EXIT=<code>` as the LAST line of dispatch.log. Check via `tail -c 300 log`, never `grep "EXIT=" log`: worker reasoning text can contain literal `EXIT=127` strings (real case: an ffmpeg PIPESTATUS note inside the transcript got picked up by a naive grep and misread as the worker's exit code). No marker AT EOF = see §silent-death below.
2. **Windows-native process check (not MSYS ps) — and the exe name is `hermes.exe`, NOT python.exe**: chat-CLI workers run as `hermes.exe` children; `wmic process where "name='python.exe'" ...` and `tasklist //FI "IMAGENAME eq python.exe"` return NOTHING useful for them. Query by exact owned PID (`wmic process where "ProcessId=<pid>" get ProcessId`) or scan `wmic process where "name='hermes.exe'" get ProcessId,CommandLine` and grep the lane signature (e.g. `t00-i02` log path embedded in the redirect).
3. **Log-size sampling**: `s1=$(stat -c%s log); sleep 30..60; s2=$(stat -c%s log)` — ANY growth = ALIVE. Zero growth proves nothing by itself; combine with the PID check above.
4. **Completion evidence trio** before declaring done: EXIT=0 marker at EOF + final-line `session_id:` + REPORT.md/STATUS present on disk.

## Silent wave death — dead WITHOUT any EXIT marker (2026-08-23 evening wave)
Distinct from false-death (§top) and from EXIT-without-REPORT (§below): BOTH parallel workers vanished mid-work and their wrappers never appended `EXIT=` — the bash wrapper itself died with them (suspected transient provider/router drop). Evidence that finally proved death (after "no marker = alive" would have waited forever):
- `wmic process where "ProcessId=<owned pid>"` → no row, across repeated checks;
- log size frozen across 2+ samples 30–60s apart;
- no `EXIT=` at EOF.
Triage order: (a) confirm all three signals above; (b) health-check the model route BEFORE resuming — `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 8 http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/models` expecting 200; (c) recover via the correction-resume pattern below with a `resume-r1.txt` whose header says RESUME-SAUKHI-CHET-AM-THAM, recaps the disk state MANAGER-VERIFIED (files actually written), and quotes the last few log lines so the worker reorients to its exact stop point; (d) `--resume <exact owner sid>`; (e) confirm revival by fresh log growth within ~60s. Both workers resumed cleanly this way. Timeline cost ≈45–60 min — budget for it in ETAs when running overnight waves.

**Revival ≠ immunity — silent deaths RECURRED the same night (2026-08-23, second vanish ~21:00).** ~90 min after the clean R1 revives above, BOTH lanes vanished again with the identical signature (no EXIT marker, logs frozen at byte-exact sizes across repeated samples, zero `ProcessId=<owned pid>` rows, no hermes/python process matches) while actively mid-test-writing. Protocol on recurrence: repeat the same triage verbatim; write `resume-r2.txt` re-recapping the stop point from FRESH disk evidence (don't reuse the r1 text — the stop point moved); `--resume` the SAME owner sid again; keep marker discipline so one dispatch.log carries the full lineage (`EXIT=`, `EXIT-R1=`, `EXIT-R2=`, …). Monitoring rule change: "growth within 60s" proves REVIVAL, not SURVIVAL — after a silent death keep sampling log delta every few minutes for the rest of the wave instead of reverting to heartbeat-only checks; two consecutive frozen samples ≥60s apart plus zero owned-PID rows = dead again. If a THIRD simultaneous death hits, stop blind-resuming: inspect router uptime/logs first and stagger/serialize the next dispatches — two concurrent streams dying together twice in one evening is a shared-route-layer pattern, not bad luck.

## Third death mode: MANAGER-BACKEND RESTART kills the whole worker tree (S13-P00-C5, 2026-08-23 evening)
Distinct signature: the Hermes desktop/backend ITSELF restarts mid-turn (app update/crash), killing every child CLI worker instantly AND wiping the manager chat's own background-process registry — `process(action='poll')` returns `not_found` for a proc id you dispatched minutes ago. Two occurrences in one evening (workers died 20:03 and ~20:40) while the route/model were healthy.
- Diagnosis trio: (a) owned pid gone from `wmic process where "name='hermes.exe'"` scan (note: desktop-app Electron children also match hermes.exe — filter by CommandLine containing `chat --resume`, not bare name); (b) dispatch.log frozen at byte-exact size across samples; (c) no EXIT marker at EOF. Same trio as silent-death, but `poll() = not_found` on a recent proc id is the giveaway that YOUR OWN backend bounced.
- Recovery identical (wait ≥5 min → resume SAME owner sid, SAME route); session history survives on disk, so nothing is lost except elapsed time. Budget each backend bounce ≈15 min (death detection + 5-min wait + resume + re-orientation).
- Multi-attempt lineage in ONE dispatch log: append, never overwrite, with round-tagged markers — `EXIT=` (attempt 1), then `EXIT_R2=$?`, `EXIT_R3=$?` … Manager log records each attempt's proc id + death evidence so Codex sees a clean chain instead of N orphaned logs.
- Partial writes across attempts are CONTINUOUS, not conflicting: attempt-2 may have written 4 of 9 deliverables before dying; attempt-3 resumes from session context and finishes the rest. Verify coverage of the FULL findings set at submit time regardless of which attempt touched which file — per-file mtimes tell you who wrote what, but the final gate greps all findings against final state only.

## EXIT code is NOT completion (2026-08-23 afternoon wave)
- I04 exited EXIT=0 cleanly but had died mid-flow BEFORE writing REPORT.md (was still patching its proof script). I01 crashed EXIT=4 mid-edit of its own test file.
- EXIT=0 only proves the CLI process ended normally — it does NOT prove the task reached TASK_SUBMITTED. Always stat for REPORT.md / STATUS marker on disk after any exit; treat missing REPORT as an incomplete worker regardless of exit code.
- EXIT=4-style crashes leave partial edits in the worker's OWN allowlist (fine to keep — attribution) plus unfinished checklist items.
- **This is a RECURRING mode, not a one-off**: T02 (EXIT=0, REPORT written ✓) but I05 and T03 both EXIT=0 with all measurements/code complete yet no REPORT.md. The resume packet for this case is the cheapest possible: header "bạn EXIT=0 nhưng chết trước khi kịp ghi REPORT", manager-verified disk-state recap (files + test results ALREADY run by manager), then ONLY remaining steps = verify coverage → write REPORT.md → LOG append → STOP. Explicitly forbid re-running benchmarks/re-measurement — the worker's own log tail already contains its final summary; quoting it back in the resume reorients instantly (~2–5 min round trip).

## Correction-resume pattern that works
When a worker dies incomplete, do NOT re-dispatch a fresh session. Instead:
0. **If the worker died mid-question, ANSWER the question in the resume packet.** Real case (T05B): worker read schemas, noticed the `RendererRoute` Literal contained placeholder values, reasoned "let me check RENDERER_ROUTES in models.py", then died. The resume packet opened by resolving exactly that: enum lives in `RENDERER_ROUTES` (models.py), five values listed inline, "dùng enum đó". A resume that reorients AND answers beats one that merely points back at files — zero wasted turns on re-derivation. Watch log tails for trailing open questions; they are free resume-packet content.
1. **Verify independently first**: run the worker's own focused suite yourself with isolated basetemp (`--basetemp=%TEMP%/mgr-check-* -p no:cacheprovider`, `env -u MOTIONFORGE_DATABASE_URL`) and capture exact assertion/integrity errors. For schema/ORM mismatches, diff constraint names mechanically — e.g. regex-extract `ck_*` names from migration file vs models.py and set-diff them; that pinpointed a migration-only `ck_structural_lock_manifest_revision_positive` in seconds.
2. **Root-cause each failure to file:line level** before writing the correction (real pairs: ORM class missing a CHECK the migration has → parity fail; test seed INSERTing duplicate PK `'rr1'` → UNIQUE fail; NVENC probe failing because 64×64 nullsrc is below NVENC min frame dimension → fix is 256×256, not "encoder missing").
3. **Write correction-r<N>.txt** listing each finding with the fix location + explicit keep/constraint list ("write-set KHÔNG ĐỔI", forbidden paths repeated), then required remaining checklist steps, ending with REPORT requirements.
4. **Resume the exact owner**: `"$HERMES" chat --provider custom --model alpha --resume <session-id> -q "$(cat correction-r1.txt)" --yolo -Q >> dispatch.log`. Append, don't overwrite: one log carries the whole lineage (initial + R1 + …) with distinct markers (`EXIT=`, `EXIT-R1=`).
5. For a worker whose core work is DONE and only REPORT/formalities are missing: the correction says explicitly "core verified PASS by manager, only do X/Y/Z then SUBMITTED" — prevents redundant rework.
6. **Manager-side verification gates that caught real bugs this wave**: run the worker's own suite twice with different basetemps for determinism (20 passed ×2); re-prove additive-only via difflib removed-lines count against the pinned baseline copy; assert single alembic head via ScriptDirectory.get_heads(); audit write-set by mtime (`find app migrations tests -newermt "<dispatch-time>" -type f -name "*.py" ! -path "*__pycache__*"`). Never accept worker-reported test counts as evidence.

## Manager verify gates that caught real bugs (2026-08-23, concrete recipes)
- **ORM↔migration parity diff by constraint name**: regex-extract `ck_*` names from the migration file and from models.py separately, set-diff them (`migration-only checks: [...]`). This pinpointed a migration-only `ck_structural_lock_manifest_revision_positive` (ORM class lacked the CHECK its migration had; sibling class had it — pattern to copy from the sibling) in seconds instead of eyeballing two giant dict dumps.
- **Duplicate-PK test seeds**: a test failing with `UNIQUE constraint failed: <table>.id` where the id is a hardcoded literal ('rr1') is a TEST bug (two seed rows sharing an explicit PK), not production. Fix = distinct ids in the seed; keep the test's intent intact.
- **NVENC probe false-negative**: h264_nvenc "unavailable" with exit 127/-22 from a lavfi probe at 64×64 is a PROBE bug — NVENC rejects frames below its minimum dimension (~145px). Fix the probe source size (256×256 nullsrc), don't conclude the encoder is missing.
- **Additive-only re-proof**: difflib unified_diff of current file vs pinned baseline copy, count lines starting `-` excluding `---` header → must be 0. Cheap, mechanical, worker-independent.
- **Write-set audit by mtime**: `find app migrations tests -newermt "<dispatch-time>" -type f -name "*.py" ! -path "*__pycache__*"` → list must equal the task allowlist exactly.

## Session-ID discovery when the log lacks it
Crashed logs may never print the trailing `session_id:` line. Fallback (worked twice this lane):
```
python -c "import sqlite3; c=sqlite3.connect(r'C:/Users/Admin/AppData/Local/hermes/state.db'); rows=c.execute('SELECT id, started_at, message_count FROM sessions WHERE started_at > <epoch> ORDER BY started_at').fetchall()"
```
Then disambiguate candidates by first user message: `SELECT content FROM messages WHERE session_id=? AND role='user' ORDER BY rowid LIMIT 1` — match on the embedded `TASK ID:` prefix. Never guess between two same-minute sessions; other manager lanes (S11 etc.) dispatch at the same minutes and their sessions interleave in the table.
- **Fresh-session dispatches also land here (2026-08-24)**: every `-q ... --pass-session-id` dispatch creates a row within seconds — if the worker dies before printing `session_id:` at EOF, query rows newer than the dispatch epoch and match on the TASK-ID prefix. This recovered owner sids for FG2 (`20260824_165139_dd1068`) and I05 (`20260823_233406_8d5b7b`) when their logs froze mid-run with no trailing marker.

## Shared-worktree parallel writers: intermediate states leak
Two writers with disjoint FILE write-sets still share runtime state. Real case: I01's half-written alembic revision made I04's conftest `_patch_project_root` fixture blow up with 27 failed/187 errors (alembic upgrade head failing mid-DDL). What worked (encode this):
- The affected worker diagnosed the foreign cause itself (mtime tracking of the migration file) and switched to a **bounded wait-loop ≤10 min/cycle**, doing useful non-blocked work (report skeleton, harness prep) between probes, then re-ran clean once the sibling settled.
- Manager note: avoid pairing a migration-WRITING task with a migration-CONSUMING test task in the same wave when feasible; if paired, warn both prompts about transient sibling state so neither blames itself nor fake-fixes around it.

## Safe-stop / supersede constraints
- Non-interactive workers (`-q ... --pass-session-id -Q`) have closed stdin: `process submit` fails ("stdin not available"). There is NO safe-stop channel.
- Therefore: do NOT dispatch production work while its scope decision is still in flight at Codex level; supersede timing must precede dispatch, not interrupt it.
- If a supersede lands mid-run: let it exit naturally, preserve every artifact for attribution (hash them), record state as TASK_SUBMITTED-theo-contract-cũ / BLOCKED pending review. Never reset/delete to "clean up".

## Session ID lineage
- Authoritative session id = the `session_id: yyyymmdd_hhmmss_hash` line printed at END of dispatch.log (matches the MSYS ps start time).
- LOG.md self-labels ("Worker session 20260823_0007") are internal run tags, NOT session ids. Registries used for resume (`--resume <sid>`) must carry the dispatch.log id or Codex resume will target nothing.

## Registry discipline on manager errors
- When a manager verdict is proven wrong later, APPEND a CORRECTION row to docs/pm/sessions/<SPRINT>-SESSION_REGISTRY.md with timestamp + root cause; never silently rewrite the earlier row. Append-only is what makes Codex attribution possible.

## Reporting & estimate discipline (user-corrected)
- User caught "Chủ nhật 25/08" (Sunday 25th) when 25 Aug was a Tuesday. NEVER derive day-of-week from memory: run `date "+%A %d/%m/%Y %H:%M %z"` and build estimate tables from that output. Write FULL dd/mm dates in every milestone row.
- User expects autonomous continuation signals ("làm toàn bộ đi", "tiếp tục đi"): don't pause for confirmation between waves once authority is granted; report progress on heartbeat and after abnormal exits only.
- Speed questions ("tách subagent tăng tốc?"): answer from the ownership rule — one Task ID = one owner session; extra speed comes ONLY from parallel disjoint lanes + read-only recon lanes, never from splitting one task across owners.
- Resource checks before parallel dispatch remain: RAM free (`wmic OS get FreePhysicalMemory`), CPU load, port availability; write-set disjointness gates production writers.

## Wave-2 task-packet pattern that produced clean parallel work
When a Codex prompt authorizes a whole sprint (T00-I01..I04 waves), the manager pre-writes per-task packets BEFORE dispatching:
- `docs/pm/sessions/<TASK-ID>-<slug>/TASK.md` — role line (provider/endpoint/model/reasoning/fallback), Bước-0 mandatory reads incl. RULES_LOADED print, current-context section stating what sibling lanes already delivered (verified facts only), outcome list, binary acceptance gates, STRICT write allowlist + FORBIDDEN list, ending protocol (LOG append → REPORT STATUS: TASK_SUBMITTED → STOP).
- `output/<run-id>/<task>/prompt.txt` — 3–5 lines only: points at the TASK.md path, repeats Bước-0 and write-set discipline. Long policy lives in TASK.md; the prompt stays tiny.
- Parallel pairing rule honored: I02 (services/adapters) ∥ I03 (scripts/fixtures) because write-sets are disjoint by construction; both depend on I01's schema which was MANAGER-VERIFIED first.
- Correction/resume files live in the same output lane (`correction-r1.txt`, `resume-r1.txt`, …) so one directory = full task history for Codex attribution.
- Sequential-chain variant (T01→T02→T03): each new TASK.md's context section cites the PREVIOUS task's manager-verified state with date, and its FORBIDDEN list grows to include everything earlier tasks now own ("reskin_* files T01 owned", "benchmark harness I03 owned — đọc thôi"). This prevented all write-set collisions across a same-night 5-task chain; each packet also pins the exact reusable entry points (`record_render_route`, adaptive_pose_swap import path) so workers integrate instead of reinventing.
- Migration-budget rule in packets: for tasks that might need schema changes, phrase as "ĐÚNG MỘT migration mới CHỈ nếu thật sự cần; nếu dùng được bảng hiện có thì KHÔNG tạo và ghi rõ quyết định trong REPORT" — T03 correctly reused job tables and skipped migration entirely under this wording.

## Resumed-owner NEW-contract pattern: TASK-SL.md, never overwrite TASK.md (2026-08-24 night)
When Codex later authorizes a RESUMED owner session for a NEW, larger scope on top of its old foundation (real case: T01 owner `b4b2ad` resumed for Source-Locked completion after its foundation got APPROVED):
- Write a SEPARATE contract file (`TASK-SL.md`) next to the original `TASK.md`; the dispatch prompt names the exact file ("đọc TASK-SL.md — KHÔNG phải TASK.md cũ"). Old TASK.md stays untouched as attribution history.
- The contract's context section lists ONLY manager-verified sibling deliverables (with verify date), states what is FORBIDDEN now that wasn't before (e.g. "KHÔNG tạo migration mới — dùng head d8e9f0a1b2c3 của I01"), and scopes ownership-transfer wiring precisely ("renderer_router.py ADDITIVE wiring only, zero removed").
- This produced a clean 1h38 resume that kept foundation 100% intact and passed every gate first try.
- Ownership-transfer wiring acceptance: diff of the wired shared file may show removed lines if imports were RELOCATED — accept only when each removed line re-appears added elsewhere in the same diff (removed == re-added count, zero net loss). Real case: router wiring showed `-RenderRequest/-RenderResult/-ROUTE_PRIORITY` but grep confirmed all 3 re-added.

## Manager-context assumptions are falsifiable — workers verify, manager re-proves (2026-08-24)
A TASK.md asserted "reference media 5A175454… KHÔNG có trên máy → SKIP_WITH_REASON". The worker found the media ON the machine (inside MAIN projects/, read-only), measured against it, and reported the assumption violation transparently in REPORT §8 instead of silently skipping or silently using it. Manager then independently re-hashed the file (`sha256` chunked read → matched expected prefix) before accepting VERIFIED status. Encode both halves: (a) task packets should phrase machine-state claims as "verify before relying"; (b) when a worker contradicts your packet, the manager must re-prove the worker right/wrong with its OWN command before updating any registry row. Worker honesty here is a pass signal, not a defect.

## Linter gates are language-scoped — don't run Python linters on web files
Running `ruff check` on a `.ts` frontend file yields hundreds of fake "invalid-syntax" errors (it parsed TypeScript as Python). Gate matrix: ruff+mypy for app/tests/scripts (.py); tsc --noEmit + eslint --max-warnings 0 for frontend (worker-gated); never cross-apply. A manager that reports "561 errors" from a wrong-linter run burns credibility — recognize and discard the run, note the mistake in the registry row if it appeared in evidence text.

## E2E-incomplete exit + CORS/port pitfall for UI tasks (2026-08-24 morning, T04)
A fourth EXIT=0 variant: worker exited cleanly mid-QA — backend suite green (9 passed, manager-verified), frontend feature built, but ONE Playwright test still red and a CORS fix just applied without rerun. For UI tasks the completion trio gains a fourth member: **E2E status**, checked before accepting SUBMITTED.
- Resume packet for this case quotes the EXACT failure evidence instead of describing it: failing test name + spec file:line + full locator + expected-vs-found, and points at the saved `error-context.md` under the task lane's `e2e-results/` dir. Explicitly forbid the two lazy "fixes": deleting/skipping the test, or bumping timeouts. Require root-cause triage between missing DOM render (component/testid bug) vs missing API payload (backend/meta bug).
- **CORS silent killer for Playwright lanes**: serving backend/dev-server on NON-default ports (real case: uvicorn :8099, frontend :3014) fails every meta fetch unless `MOTIONFORGE_CORS_ORIGINS` includes those exact origins — the downstream symptom is `element(s) not found` on data-driven sections, which masquerades as a component bug and costs a debugging turn. UI-task packets should pre-pin ports AND the matching CORS env in the setup/Bước-0 section.
- After a mid-QA fix, instruct "rerun the FULL spec across all projects (desktop+mobile)", not just the failing test — project-level ordering means single-test reruns hide order-dependent failures.

## OpenAPI path-count additive gate (cheap contract check)
After any API-touching task: boot the app and count — `len(app.openapi()['paths'])`, plus filtered list for the feature prefix. Additive-only acceptance = total count increased, zero pre-existing paths removed (219→221 T01, 221→229 T03). Catches accidental route deletion in seconds without diffing giant spec dumps. Pair with `openapi_paths_before.txt` snapshot saved in the task output lane BEFORE dispatch so the comparison baseline is pinned, not remembered.

## Measured-benchmark determinism & freeze gates (Wave-2 verify, 2026-08-23 night)
How the manager verified I03 (benchmark harness) and accepted its two seeded runs — patterns reusable for any measured-results acceptance:
1. **Never whole-file-hash two runs of a benchmark**: strip the harness's DECLARED non-deterministic fields first, then compare cores. Real case: raw JSON hashes differed between seed-identical runs, but the results file declared `"non_deterministic_fields_excluded_from_compare": ["wall_runtime_ms_per_frame", "vram_peak_mib"]`; after stripping those keys, cores were byte-identical → determinism PASS. A harness that does NOT declare its non-deterministic fields is itself a finding.
2. **Freeze-before-measure must be test-enforced**: frozen SHA banner (schema_version=1 + per-component SHA256 of harness/fixtures/thresholds) printed BEFORE any measurement line; a dedicated test (`test_freeze_banner_printed_before_measure`) locks that ordering. Every measured artifact embeds the same frozen SHA — verify it matches at gate time, don't trust the worker's quote of it.
3. **Cross-run skip-path inconsistencies get recorded, not normalized**: run1 wrote probe metadata into `reference_evaluation` where run2 wrote only the skip-reason string (verified-reference media absent from machine). Don't silently reconcile either way — registry evidence note for Codex review; hiding it reads as tampering later.
4. **Prove benchmarks are REAL via artifacts**: bench .mp4 outputs on disk, results JSON carries concrete measurements (ms/frame, VRAM bytes, license ids like `ffmpeg-gpl-build`) — not just `"ok": true`. Placeholder-shaped evidence fails manager verify.
5. **I05-style measurement-task packet**: write-allowlist = output lane only (+LOG/REPORT in session dir); REPORT separates MEASURED / UNKNOWN / SKIPPED; forbid post-hoc threshold tuning and forbid recomputing metrics not present in raw results (mark UNKNOWN instead).

## Empty-content deaths at session start — shrink the resume packet, don't resend the fat prompt (2026-08-24 midday, T06B)
A fifth death signature appeared on the FINAL task: worker exits almost immediately (log 11KB), tail shows `⚠️ No reply: the model returned empty content after retries and any fallback providers` right after a batch-read plan. The R1 resume then died THE SAME WAY at 34KB — again empty-content, again mid-batch-read.
- Router `/v1/models` stayed 200 throughout; a direct `/v1/chat/completions` probe may even return an auth error without credentials — neither proves the chat path is healthy for long reasoning turns. Treat router health checks as necessary-not-sufficient.
- Deaths clustered during large batched reads early in a resumed turn of a BIG session → suspicion: oversized context assembly on resume.
- **What worked (R2)**: stop resending the original full TASK prompt; send a SHORT reorientation packet — "Tiếp tục đúng chỗ dở: bạn đang batch-read X/Y/Z. Sau đó làm phần còn lại theo TASK.md <path>: <one-line deliverable summary>. Write-set đúng allowlist. Kết thúc STATUS: TASK_SUBMITTED rồi STOP." Log grew immediately (+16KB within 75s) and the worker progressed into real analysis. Full detail: `references/empty-content-resume-pattern.md`.
- Rule of thumb: after two consecutive empty-content deaths, shrink the resume packet to a pointer at TASK.md plus a two-line where-were-you recap. The session history already carries details; the packet only needs to restart the loop.
- Keep marker discipline across all attempts in ONE dispatch.log (`EXIT=`, `EXIT-R1=`, `EXIT-R2=` …) and record each attempt's proc id + death evidence in the registry row so Codex sees the attempt chain.
- **Empty-content also hits FRESH sessions and recurs across an entire evening (2026-08-24 afternoon→evening, T06B + FG2)**: it is NOT resume-only. T06B died on its FIRST dispatch; FG2's fresh dispatch died at 764KB mid-edit after fixing only 2 of 4 files, then AGAIN on the next dispatch. When one lane takes 3+ empty-content deaths in an evening while other lanes run fine: (a) shrink every subsequent prompt/resume to the pointer-packet form; (b) instruct workers "mỗi bước ghi log ngay để không mất tiến độ" so each surviving window banks progress; (c) expect per-death cost ~15–20 min and add that to ETAs honestly instead of pretending the timeline holds; (d) manager probes (`/v1/models` 200) do NOT predict chat-path health — stop treating a 200 as "router fine, must be the worker".
- **Endgame validation (FG2 R1, 2026-08-24 evening)**: the pointer-packet pattern closed out the worst lane of the night — FG2's resume-r1 enumerated the EXACT remaining failures (file:line, keep-literal vs switch-to-live-discovery classification, named the already-passing sibling as copy-template) and the worker returned 18 passed ×2 with zero hard-coded new-head strings. The full-sprint end state arrived the same evening: regression run 3 = **1760 passed / 0 failed / 19 skipped EXIT=0**, sprint declared SPRINT_SUBMITTED / MANAGER_VERIFIED_PENDING_CODEX_REVIEW at 20:45+07. Pattern held through the finish line.

## Sprint-chain endgame patterns (2026-08-24, T05A→T06B — last 4 tasks of an 11-task sprint)
- **Manager verify caught a partially-red submission (T05A: 3 failed / 33 passed)** that the worker's EXIT=0 hid. The resume packet enumerated the three failing tests by name with failure class per test ("sửa test seed HOẶC handler bug tùy nguyên nhân thật — không fake pass") plus the exact half-finished fix the worker had described in its own log tail. Result: clean 36/36 ×2 on next exit. Never let "EXIT=0" + a mostly-green suite substitute for running the suite yourself before either accepting or writing the correction.
- **Migration round-trip gate has a legitimate blocker**: downgrade-to-base failed with `RuntimeError: Character library migration is not reversible per S06 contract` — a BY-DESIGN earlier-sprint contract, not a defect of the new revision. Correct verification scope for a new revision on top of irreversible history: round-trip `head ↔ <parent-of-new-revision>` only (here head↔d8e9f0a1b2c3), and record WHY base-downgrade is out of scope so Codex doesn't read the skip as evasion.
- **"No new migration needed" is itself a verified outcome** (T03 reused job tables; T06A found ApplyCheckpoint foundation already sufficient): both packets pre-authorized it ("migration CHỈ nếu thật sự cần; nếu dùng được bảng hiện có thì KHÔNG tạo và ghi quyết định vào REPORT"), both workers skipped cleanly, heads stayed pinned (`d8e9f0a1b2c3` then `b3c4d5e6f7a9`). Manager still re-ran `ScriptDirectory.get_heads()` at verify time rather than trusting the REPORT claim.
- **Final-task packet (T06B) front-loads the whole chain**: context section cites every prior task's manager-verified state WITH date, names the exact reusable artifacts (`CorrectionPanel.tsx`, global-setup idempotent pattern, QA port pattern :8099/:3014), and the acceptance gate includes "backend T06A suites rerun 1 lần confirm xanh" so the last worker proves it didn't break predecessors. The final task is where cross-task regressions would otherwise surface after everyone has exited.
- **Worker self-quality signal worth crediting in heartbeat reports** (T05B): worker proactively refactored DERIVED state when newer eslint react-hooks rules flagged `Math.random`-in-render / setState-in-effect — report these as pass signals to the user, they justify the alpha-route investment.
- **Terminal-state write must go through file tools, not heredoc**: appending the sprint terminal-state block via `cat >> file << 'EOF'` in a foreground `terminal()` call got hard-blocked by the shell guard ("appears to start a long-lived server/watch process") — heredocs trip long-command heuristics. Use the `patch` tool (old_string = an existing unique anchor line in the report, new_string = anchor + the new block). This also keeps the append atomic and reviewable.

## Final-gate stale-allowlist test: the failure class NO task allowlist owned (2026-08-24, FG1)
The first full-regression run of the final gate failed on `test_durable_job_persistence.py::test_no_worker_or_api_cutover_tables` — a hardcoded table allowlist from the S02/S08 era missing 6 additive tables (`reskin_config`, `apply_checkpoint`, `s09_correction`, `segment_render_route`, `structural_lock_manifest`, `project_cast_mapping`). Root cause of the gap: **schema-hardcoding regression tests that no worker's write allowlist covered** — I04 normalized exactly 6 named files, and this 7th sibling was outside every packet. Lessons:
1. **Expect exactly this failure at the first full gate after any schema-touching sprint**: grep candidate regression files for hardcoded expected-table sets BEFORE the gate (`grep -ln "unexpected tables" tests/*.py` finds them all), and either fold them into the I04-style normalization task's allowlist up front or pre-authorize a narrow FG-correction lane.
2. **FG correction lane pattern** (worked end-to-end in ~20 min): TASK.md scoped to ONE file + "copy the normalized pattern from tests/test_persistence_bootstrap.py", acceptance = ×2 PASS + adversarial proof (plant `sneaky_unknown_table_*` into a COPY db → assertion must flag exactly it; clean DB → PASS). Worker produced `adversarial_proof.log`; manager re-ran the suite twice with own basetemps to confirm.
3. **Attribution framing for Codex**: even when part of the gap predates the sprint (2 tables existed at sprint start), record it as "pre-existing gap that I04's allowlist MISSED — still must fix, not excuse". Never let a real gate failure be dismissed as pre-existing without the fix dispatched.
4. **Full-regression runs MUST go background with output redirect into a PRE-CREATED dir**: foreground 600s timeout kills the run mid-suite (~5–8 min total), and redirecting `> <dir>/log` before `mkdir -p <dir>` fails instantly ("No such file or directory") — the bash-level failure looks like the suite refused to start. Sequence: mkdir first (separate command is fine), then background dispatch appending `EXIT=$?` marker as usual.

## Final gate continued: FG2/FG3 — the stale-assertion debt comes in WAVES (2026-08-24 evening)
FG1 fixed one file, but the full gate then surfaced TWO MORE waves of the same disease. Encode the full sequence so the next sprint doesn't rediscover it:
1. **NEVER run the final-gate full regression with `-x`** — the first run stopped at the first failure (238 passed / 1 failed / 1526 cleanup-errors in 5 min) and HID everything downstream. The unrestricted run 2 (27:45, backgrounded, ~1750 tests) then surfaced 6 more stale-assertion failures plus proved run 1's 1526 "errors" were Windows PermissionError noise from pytest's own basetemp rmtree (`WinError 32` on sqlite handles) — infrastructure cleanup noise, NOT test failures; judge by FAILED lines only. Budget ~30 min per full run and always background it.
2. **Re-grep for stale allowlists/head-constants AFTER EVERY mid-sprint schema addition**, not once at the gate. T05A adding migration `b3c4d5e6f7a9` retroactively broke 7 test files across three waves (FG1: hardcoded table set; FG2: 4 files with `HEAD = "<old-rev>"` constants incl. two still pinning `b2c3d4e5f6a7b` from BEFORE the sprint; FG3: bootstrap `S08_HEAD_TABLES` missing the brand-new `s09_correction` table + two more S08-A01 files with the same stale HEAD constant). Cheap sweeps: `grep -ln "unexpected tables" tests/*.py` and `grep -n "^HEAD\s*=\|^HEAD_REVISION" tests/*migration*.py`.
3. **Partial-fix resume (FG2 pattern)**: worker died model-empty having fixed 2/4 files (verified: those now PASS). Resume packet enumerated the EXACT remaining 5 failures with file:line, split each into "revision-identity assert — KEEP the literal (it tests that specific migration)" vs "head-position assert — switch to live `ScriptDirectory.get_heads()`", named the already-passing sibling file as the copy-template, and banned hard-coding the NEW head too. Result: 18 passed ×2 next exit. Verify loop after ANY such resume: rerun the touched files ×2 with fresh basetemps + `ruff` + confirm zero occurrences of the new head string in tests (`grep -c b3c4… = 0`) and ≥1 `get_heads` usage per file.
4. **Static gates fill the regression-run wait window**: while the ~30-min background suite runs, clear the cheap gates in foreground — `ruff check app tests`, `mypy app` (124 files), `ScriptDirectory.get_heads()` single-head assert, frontend `npx tsc --noEmit`. All four passed untouched in one pass because every task packet had enforced them per-task; if any fails here, the offending task's REPORT lied and gets reopened.
5. **MAIN-unchanged check is signature-scoped, not "zero dirty"**: the protected MAIN tree legitimately carries ~91 dirty paths from OTHER lanes (docs/pm prompts, handoffs, automation config written by Codex/S11/S13 sessions). The correct assertion: `git status --porcelain | grep -E "<this-sprint's-file-signatures>"` (reskin|structural|s09_|renderer_r|demo…) must return EMPTY, and mtime histogram of dirty files shows nothing newer than your dispatch window in app/**. A blanket "dirty count changed" alarm fires on sibling lanes' paperwork and wastes a triage cycle.

6. **Endgame confirmation (2026-08-24 20:35)**: after FG1+FG2+FG3 landed, the next unrestricted run came back fully green — **1760 passed / 0 failed / 19 skipped, EXIT=0 (27:59)** (`regression-run3.log`). The stale-assertion debt proved FINITE: three narrow corrections cleared all of it. Declare the gate complete only on an unrestricted zero-failed run AFTER the last fix lands — per-file ×2 passes alone are necessary, not sufficient.

## CHANGES_REQUESTED → fast-track correction round (2026-08-24 evening, S09-C1)

When Codex returns `CHANGES_REQUESTED` with findings F1..Fn and authorizes a fast-track multi-worker correction prompt (real case: `S09_C1_FAST_TRACK_MANAGER_2026-08-24.md`, max 5 workers + join gates J1/J2), follow the full execution record in `references/s09-c1-fast-track-round.md` — timeline, lock table, packet texts, hash recipe. Compressed rules:

1. **Startup sequence**: re-read rules fresh (mandatory), then the REVIEW RECORD itself (`docs/pm/reviews/<sprint>_REVIEW_<date>.md`) — findings there are the source of truth, each with P0/P1 level, owner Task ID, deferred-vs-blocking status. Map every finding to its owning session before writing anything.
2. **Owner-existence preflight before ANY dispatch**: query state.db for every exact session id named in the Codex prompt (`SELECT id FROM sessions WHERE id=?`) AND disambiguate each by its first user message matching the expected TASK ID prefix. Real case: all 11 named sessions verified EXISTS + correct task in one batch — prevented resuming a wrong same-minute session.
3. **Lock-table registry before dispatch** (`docs/pm/sessions/<SPRINT>-C1-SESSION-REGISTRY.md`, Manager-owned): task → exact session → phase → proc id (filled after dispatch) → state → exclusive write-set summary → hot-file SHA256-prefixes captured BEFORE workers start → dependencies. Workers only ever append their own LOG/REPORT; the manager is sole writer of the registry.
4. **Per-correction packets mirror the review language**: quote the finding ID (F1/F5/…) inline so the worker knows exactly which review bullet it fixes; restate acceptance as binary checks; make NEW restrictions explicit ("KHÔNG mount app", "KHÔNG sửa app/api/app.py trước J2").
5. **Join-gate waves** (real: J1 renderer-contract freeze, J2 production-API integration): the dependent worker's packet states explicitly which capability unlocks later ("measured run chỉ làm ở Wave B sau J1"; "LƯU Ý J2: Manager sẽ resume lại session này cho phase T56-INTEGRATION"). The finishing worker marks `CONTRACT_FROZEN` in its REPORT; the manager then hashes the frozen artifact (SHA-256 prefixes into the registry) and announces the gate name before unlocking the next lane. Only ONE worker per shared file across the whole round — later phases get the app.py write-lock granted back to the SAME owner session, never a second owner.
6. **Out-of-authority reconciliation under Codex scrutiny (F7)**: if earlier corrections happened outside the authorized task map, the registry carries their EXACT session ids (query state.db to confirm each), states plainly that authority was not retroactive ("không hợp thức hóa authority"), and keeps their fixes on disk pending Codex decision. Never invent new task IDs post-hoc to legalize them.
7. **Conditional-resume lanes**: some owners (real case T05B) resume ONLY IF the production-stack test proves a failure belongs uniquely to them; shared files get per-turn locks with a default integration owner. Write these rules into the registry at round start, not ad hoc mid-wave.
8. **Round-specific terminal vocabulary**: fast-track prompts define their own terminal strings (`S09-C1 = TASK_MANAGER_VERIFIED / PENDING_CODEX_REVIEW` or `BLOCKED_WITH_FINDINGS / PENDING_CODEX_REVIEW`) — use the prompt's exact spelling in the final report, then STOP unconditionally.
9. **Verify-as-they-exit cadence + mechanical join gates** (from the actual Wave A run): the moment a proc notifies complete, run its focused suites ×2 with fresh basetemps and append the timestamped registry row IMMEDIATELY — T06A-C1 (~22:51), T05A-C1 (~23:41), I03-PREP (~23:50) each verified within minutes while siblings kept coding; batching verifies to wave-end would have delayed J2 by hours. Join conditions ("both verified AND exited") are read straight off registry rows + proc table — dispatch the dependent phase (T56-INTEGRATION as a second `--resume` of the SAME owner with an `EXIT-T56=` lineage marker in the same dispatch.log) the moment they read green. The previously-forbidden shared file's write-lock transfers BACK to the session that already owned the feature, never a second owner.

## Gate-end manager cleanup (temp dirs + process sweep)
After the green run: workers have already exited — do NOT kill anything; instead sweep pytest basetemp dirs left by every manager verify pass:
```
for d in $(ls "$LOCALAPPDATA/Temp" | grep -E 'mgr-|s09t0|s09fg'); do rm -rf "$LOCALAPPDATA/Temp/$d" 2>/dev/null; done
```
- Run it in BATCHES: many dirs are Windows-file-locked on the first pass (lingering sqlite handles); they only delete on later attempts. Loop until the grep count returns 0 (took 2–3 batches for ~445 dirs this lane).
- Locked stragglers are throwaway (%TEMP%) — a verified 0-remaining count just makes the handoff evidence unambiguous.
- Also confirm zero live `pytest|uvicorn|playwright` processes: `wmic process where "name='python.exe'" get ProcessId,CommandLine | grep -cE "pytest|uvicorn|playwright"` expecting 0.
- Record the cleanup numbers (dirs swept, procs remaining, DB URL UNSET) in the sprint report's terminal-state block so Codex sees closure, not assertion.

## Fast-track round MID-WAVE execution (S09-C1 Wave A, 2026-08-24 night — 5 parallel owners)

Running an authorized 5-worker correction round taught the between-dispatch-and-terminal patterns:

1. **Verify each worker AS IT EXITS, never batch**: the moment a proc notifies complete, run its focused suites ×2 with fresh basetemps, append the timestamped registry row immediately, then return to monitoring. Real cadence: T06A-C1 exited ~22:51 (26 passed ×2), T05A-C1 ~23:41 (28 passed ×2 + a NEW 39-test validation file), I03-C1-PREP ~23:50 (26 passed ×2) — each verified within minutes while sibling lanes kept coding. Batching verifies until wave-end would have delayed the J2 gate by hours.
2. **Join-gate conditions are MECHANICAL checks, not judgment calls**: J2 required "T05A-C1 và T06A-C1 đều TASK_MANAGER_VERIFIED và process đã exit" — both readable straight from registry rows + proc table. Dispatch the dependent phase the moment conditions read green; do not wait for the rest of the wave or the next heartbeat.
3. **Opening a join gate = phase-2 resume of the SAME owner session**: J2 was executed as a SECOND `--resume 20260824_120141_312e9e` with a short phase-packet ("PHASE 2 — S09-T56-INTEGRATION-C1 (J2 đã mở...)…"), appending `EXIT-T56=$?` marker lineage into the SAME dispatch.log. The previously-forbidden file's write-lock (app/api/app.py) transfers BACK to the session that already owned the feature — never granted to a second owner.
5. **Commit-semantics verification (F4) is LOCATION-sensitive**: grepping `.commit()` inside the SERVICE returned 0 and could be misread as "defect persists" — the correct fix placed `session.commit()` in the ROUTE layer strictly AFTER all validation, wrapped in try/except→rollback ("nothing was persisted"), with a replay-path rollback too so no accidental write crosses the request boundary. Verify by reading the route handler's control flow, not by counting commit calls per layer. Durable-reload evidence means the test builds its own `create_session_factory(engine)` — dependency-override auto-commit masks exactly this bug.
6. **Static-analysis errors can be a SIBLING's in-flight edit, not your defect (T56/T02 overlap)**: during T56's verify, mypy flagged `s09_demo_jobs.py:203 "object" not callable` — a line T56 never touched. Cause: T02-C1 was STILL RUNNING and editing `select_route()`'s return type inside its own write-set (`renderer_routes/**`). Rule: before attributing a NEW static error to the just-finished worker, check whether the erroring line CALLS a symbol owned by a STILL-RUNNING worker; if yes, record the attribution in the registry row ("sẽ resolve khi sibling exit"), keep the finished task VERIFIED, and add the re-check to the final-gate checklist.

## Persistent mypy error AFTER the sibling exits — PEP 562 lazy re-export kills static types (S09-C1 endgame)

If the flagged line STILL fails mypy once the owning worker exits, it becomes a REAL cross-task defect owned by whoever introduced the pattern. Real case: T02-C1 rewrote `app/services/renderer_routes/__init__.py` to PEP 562 lazy re-export (`def __getattr__(name) -> object` with an import inside) to break an adapter⇄package circular import. Runtime was correct, but every STATIC importer of the lazily-re-exported symbols (`from app.services.renderer_routes import select_route` in T03-owned `s09_demo_jobs.py`) now typed as `object` → `"object" not callable` at the call site. The call-site file is unowned-by-you, so the fix MUST land in the file that introduced the pattern.
- **Fix that passed**: keep runtime `__getattr__` unchanged; add a `if TYPE_CHECKING:` block in the same `__init__.py` importing the real symbols from their home module — mypy uses the TYPE_CHECKING branch for static importers, runtime keeps the lazy path. Result: `mypy app --no-incremental` went 1 error → Success in 125 files; the importing task's tests stayed green untouched.
- Verify loop after such a fix: `mypy app --no-incremental` (0 errors), plus rerun BOTH the fixed package's suites AND a downstream consumer suite (demo-loops) to prove the runtime lazy path still works — 47 passed in one run here.
- General rule for packets: any task introducing `__getattr__`-based re-exports must state so in its REPORT and pre-run `mypy app --no-incremental`, because the breakage only appears in OTHER tasks' files at the next full gate.

## Honest FAIL_OPEN_QUESTION closes a measured-decision round without blocking (I05-C1)

A measurement task whose frozen contract legitimately rejects some fixtures should record the gap, not fake coverage. I05-C1's runs showed `measured_state: CONTRACT_REJECTED_BY_FROZEN_CONTRACT` for 2 of 6 risk classes (hard_cut: no route accepted that contract shape; group_occlusion: sprite_affine fail-closed missing z-order, pose_swap doesn't take prop_trajectory). Worker wrote them up as explicit **FOQ-1 / FOQ-2 open questions for Codex** ("mở tham số z → phải hash handshake lại contract?" / "f5 ngoài phạm vi renderer hiện tại?") and still ended STATUS: TASK_SUBMITTED. Manager verified determinism mechanically before accepting: strip declared non-deterministic fields `[wall_runtime_ms_per_frame, vram_peak_mib]` PLUS per-result `artifact_path`/`adversarial_artifact` (they differ between run dirs by design — different output directories), then require zero core diffs. Encode: (a) measurement-task packets should pre-authorize FAIL_OPEN_QUESTION wording exactly like migration-budget wording ("thiếu evidence → ghi FAIL_OPEN_QUESTION, không tự mở downstream"); (b) determinism comparison strips declared-telemetry + run-local artifact paths, nothing else; (c) honest partial-measured rounds are a VERIFY-PASS, and the open questions become review-queue items for Codex rather than silent debt.

## Join-gate handshake hashes need a REPRODUCIBLE RECIPE (J1 renderer-contract freeze)

T02-C1 froze its public contract with `CONTRACT_FROZEN: SHA-256 = 46c6a41f…bbc1e`, listing the three hashed files ("bytes của renderer_contract.py + renderer_routes/__init__.py + composite.py") but NOT the derivation formula. The manager's reproduction attempts failed serially — raw byte concat ✗, per-file-hex concat/newline/spaced ✗, LF-normalized ✗, adding router as 4th file ✗ — before systematic enumeration found the actual recipe: **per-file `sha256(utf8(path) + b'\0' + file_bytes)` chained in the listed order** (full digest matched exactly).

Rules:
1. Freeze-style markers MUST state the recipe inline (`sha256(path\0content, per file, theo thứ tự liệt kê)`), never just file names + a digest. A hash the next party cannot reproduce is not a handshake, it's a claim.
2. When reproducing an unknown recipe, enumerate combos SYSTEMATICALLY instead of guessing once and giving up: raw concat → per-file-hex joins (concat/newline/space) → path\0content chains → LF normalization → sibling-file inclusion. Budget 2–3 minutes; the path\0content family wins often because it binds filenames into the digest (detects renames).
3. The handshake completes only on FULL-digest equality — prefix or "close enough" is not acceptable for a gate that locks other workers out of modifying those files.
5. **Workers invent NEW test files beyond the packet's named patterns** (T05A-C1 added `tests/test_s09_t05_backend_c1_validation.py`, 39 tests): when verifying "adversarial coverage exists", DISCOVER the lane's test files first (`ls tests/test_s09_t05_backend_*`) instead of grepping only the originally-named files — the naive grep reported 0 adversarial patterns and nearly reopened a passing finding. Same trap for docstrings: after "remove stale literals", `grep direct_composite` still hits once — inside the comment explaining the removal. Confirm a hit is documentation, not code, before reopening anything.

## Wave-B overlap dispatch: start the successor lane while the finished lane polishes gates (I03 gates ∥ T06B dispatch, 2026-08-25 03:15)

When the dependent lane's REMAINING work is non-overlapping polish (lint/mypy/REPORT formality) and the new lane's write-set is disjoint (frontend/e2e specs vs benchmark script), dispatch the join-gate successor IMMEDIATELY instead of serializing behind cosmetic cleanup — I03's gate cleanup and T06B-C1's production-stack E2E ran simultaneously with zero coordination cost. The serialization instinct comes from treating "TASK_MANAGER_VERIFIED" as the unlock point, but the prompt's actual unlock condition was J2 (both backend corrections verified + exited), already satisfied an hour earlier. Read join-gate conditions LITERALLY; never add unstaged ordering. Related: when the finishing worker exits mid-gates (sixth exit variant), freeze its measured artifacts in the resume packet ("results GIỮ NGUYÊN — không đo lại") so an eager worker doesn't re-run the benchmark just to make gates pass cleanly.

## S09-C2 round addenda (2026-08-25 morning/afternoon — seventh exit variant + schema-bump lie)

1. **Seventh EXIT variant: "TASK_SUBMITTED over a RED suite"** — I03-C2-PREP exited 0 with STATUS: TASK_SUBMITTED while its own harness suite was 8 failed / 21 passed: it bumped `SCHEMA_VERSION = 3` in the benchmark script but left fixture `thresholds.json` at version 2, so every subprocess test fail-closed (`thresholds schema_version must be 3, got 2`). The report cited gate logs that didn't cover this. Rule: run the focused suite YOURSELF before accepting any SUBMITTED — a green STATUS line is evidence of nothing. Packet-level prevention: every PREP prompt now carries "bump của SCHEMA_VERSION/policy constant nào phải bump CẢ mọi fixture/data file mang version đó trong cùng một change; threshold VALUES thì KHÔNG được tune."

Resume packet named the exact mismatch + remaining steps → one-shot fix (`func.lower(Job.job_type)`), Chromium ×2 passed on the next exit. Don't treat early-exit as done, and don't spawn a replacement session either.
3. **Cross-lane findings go to the REGISTRY for the owning lane** — T06B surfaced two defects outside its write-set (CorrectionPanel doesn't send `affected_loop_ids`; ApprovalPanel `reasonsOf` can never match route_override corrections because the payload lacks `request.reasons`). Record them in the registry row attributed to T05B; do NOT let the reporting worker "helpfully" fix them.

Same pattern as the artifacts/artifacts duplication check. One explanatory comment mentioning the removed thing is fine; an executable branch is not.
6. **New worker-created test files get missed by old focused-suite commands** — T02-C2 added `tests/test_s09_t02_c2_timebase_identity_contract.py`; the pre-existing focused invocation didn't include it. Discover lane test files fresh (`ls tests/test_s09_t02_*`) at verify time instead of reusing the packet's original file list.

## Stacked same-owner resumes: track PROCS, not lanes (S09-C3 night, 2026-08-26)

Multi-phase correction rounds resume the SAME owner session repeatedly (PREP → FINAL → BINDING), and each phase is its own background proc with its own EXIT marker (`EXIT-T04PREP=` / `EXIT-T04FINAL=` / `EXIT-T04BIND=` — markers worked perfectly). The trap: **completion notifications can lag HOURS behind reality** — T04's PREP proc (dispatched 23:47) only delivered its notification at ~04:01, AFTER the manager had already stacked FINAL (~02:20) and BINDING (02:28) on the same sid. Consequences observed: PREP and FINAL both died exit=1 mid-diff with no summary (suspected interleaved session-history appends between concurrent `hermes chat --resume <same-sid>` processes), while BINDING survived and carried the work.

Rules encoded:
1. **Before dispatching phase N+1 to an owner, `process(action='poll')` EVERY prior live proc of that owner** — never treat "no notification yet" as "still running", and never treat a heartbeat row labeled by LANE as proof of a single live proc. A lane can have several live procs after stacked resumes.
2. **If a later round survives while earlier rounds died exit=1 mid-work, do NOT re-dispatch the dead attempts** — the same session's newest turn supersedes their scope (its context includes everything they read/wrote). Verify the survivor's coverage at submit time against the FULL packet checklist instead.
3. Exit=1 + log ending abruptly right after a diff dump + no trailing summary = died mid-turn, NOT a contract violation. Record it as such in the registry; the retry decision follows liveness evidence below, not the exit code alone.

## Process-tree CPU probe: log frozen + no notification ≠ dead (Windows recipe)

When a worker's dispatch.log freezes across samples AND its notification hasn't arrived, walk the process tree from the dispatcher bash PID down to the leaf python and sample CPU — this resolved the T04-BINDING case in one pass while log sat frozen 80s:
```
powershell -Command "Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ParentProcessId=<bash-pid>' | Select ProcessId,Name"
# repeat walking down: bash.exe → bash.exe (-lic …chat --resume…) → hermes.exe (chat --resume <owner>) → python.exe
powershell -Command "(Get-Process -Id <leaf-python-pid>).CPU"   # sample twice 60–90s apart
```
- **Leaf CPU increasing = ALIVE**, even with byte-frozen logs — the worker was mid long-reasoning/API turn (real case: CPU 9.23s → 9.59s, log then grew +4KB).
- Confirm identity by reading the hermes.exe CommandLine (must contain the exact `--resume <owner-sid>` you care about — desktop-app Electron children also show as hermes-related).
- Router health stays necessary-not-sufficient: `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:20128/v1/models` returning 200 does not prove the worker's chat path is progressing; the CPU/log-delta pair is the real signal.
- Only after ALL of (log frozen ≥2 samples, leaf CPU static, tree gone/poll-not-found) declare death and start the 5-minute wait → same-owner resume cycle.
